lines.text: For five seconds nothing on Earth can grip anything, and Gus slides twenty feet without taking a step.
It's nine on a Sunday morning and Gus is shoving a heavy flowerpot across his garden.
It scrapes and sticks and he wishes friction would just go away.
His wife says he'd miss it. His neighbor says life would be a breeze.
Then for five seconds Gus gets his wish.
The pot glides off like a puck on ice. But his feet can't push, so he runs on the spot.
His wife's cup slips right through her fingers and the neighbor's ladder slides flat down the wall.
Then the whole garden starts to drift, all the same way.
But the lawn looks flat. So what's pulling them?
You see, no lawn is flat. Builders tilt it half an inch a foot so rain runs away from the house.
That slope tugs at Gus with nine pounds all day long.
Ever pressed two brushes together? Up close his feet and the grass are bristles too, and they lock.
Take that away and nine pounds is plenty. Heavy or light, everything speeds up alike: twenty feet in five seconds.
Unluckily it grabs his feet and the rest of Gus keeps going at a jogging pace.
And his pot? It stops twenty feet too far.
Gus drags it all the way back and never complains again.
